relations: The descending press head gradually compresses the pile of shattered ceramic shards.
Compression of the shard pile ejects curved fragments sideways and downward.
The lowest decorated bowl remains centered and largely intact beneath the compressing shards.
caption: The video captures a close, static shot of a crushing setup, where a large cylindrical metal press head sits above a yellow-and-black striped base. Between them lies a stack of white ceramic bowls decorated with a peach-like fruit and red characters; the upper bowls are already reduced to a jumble of curved shards, while the lowest decorated bowl remains mostly whole. The press head descends only slightly and gradually, pressing further into the shard pile. As it presses, the broken shards shift and compress, ejecting fragments sideways and downward, with a curved white piece tumbling out on the right and fine debris streaking on the left. The lower bowl's rim sheds no chips and develops no visible new crack; all flying fragments come from the shattered upper pile. The lower bowl stays centered and largely intact, its surface pattern fixed relative to the base throughout.
